The bill would let the minister declare an exceptional circumstance, such as the ongoing effects of the Middle East conflict, to help businesses respond to situations that are not a national emergency.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) could then authorise or exempt conduct that serves the public interest but would normally break competition laws, as long as it helps with the response.
The new powers include safeguards to protect consumers, and declarations can be disallowed and will expire after a set period; the bill starts the day after royal assent.
Gives the minister power to make an exceptional circumstance declaration.
Enables the ACCC to authorise or exempt conduct that breaches competition laws if it is in the public interest and assists the response.
Adds safeguards including consumer protection, disallowance, and sunset provisions for declarations.
Businesses responding to exceptional circumstances that are not a national emergency under the NED Act.

The bill would let spouses voluntarily split their superannuation balances each year to reduce the gender super gap.
A partner with a higher balance could roll over an amount to their spouse, up to a limit that brings the smaller balance to no more than the general transfer balance cap.
The mechanism would not apply to defined benefit schemes or to people in pension phase, and would be available only to those with a single superannuation account.
Amends the Superannuation Industry (Supervision) Act 1993, the Superannuation Industry (Supervision) Regulations 1994 and the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997.
Creates a voluntary annual mechanism for couples to evenly split superannuation balances.
Limits roll overs to the spousal redistribution limit, which is the amount that would bring the smaller balance to the general transfer balance cap.
Requires that the split amount retains its original contribution characteristics and taxed or untaxed proportions.
Treats the amount received as a roll over superannuation benefit, not a new contribution, so it does not attract new taxes.
Spouses with superannuation accounts, particularly those with unequal balances, and those who have only one superannuation account.

Customs Legislation Amendment (False Trade Marks Infringement Notices) Bill 2026

Moved the second reading of a bill creating a strict liability offence for importing goods with false trade marks and enabling infringement notices. The measure responds to over 700,000 counterfeit items seized in the 2024-25 financial year, supports enforcement by the Australian Border Force and aims to protect consumers and legitimate businesses.
Treasury Laws Amendment (Supporting Choice in Superannuation and Other Measures) Bill 2025

Moved procedural motions to suspend standing orders, put questions, and limit consideration of the Treasury Laws Amendment (Supporting Choice in Superannuation and Other Measures) Bill 2025 to 60 minutes.
Parliamentary Frameworks Legislation Amendment (Reviews) Bill 2026

Moved the Parliamentary Frameworks Legislation Amendment (Reviews) Bill 2026, which would combine statutory reviews of parliamentary workplace legislation into a broader review and align future reviews of the Parliamentary Workplace Support Service Act 2023 and Parliamentary Business Resources Act 2017.
Royal Commissions Legislation Amendment (Protections for Providing Information) Bill 2026

Moved that the Royal Commissions Legislation Amendment (Protections for Providing Information) Bill 2026 be read a second time, arguing it would create an enduring framework for Royal Commissions to receive sensitive intelligence and operational information, protect people who provide it from secrecy-offence liability, and prevent secrecy provisions from being used to refuse evidence.
Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Amendment Bill (No. 2) 2025

Moved bills to make ASIO's compulsory questioning powers permanent and broaden their application while strengthening safeguards and oversight, expand National Immunisation Program access to passive immunological products, and make technical social security and veterans' affairs amendments ahead of 1 July 2026.
National Disability Insurance Scheme Amendment (Integrity and Safeguarding) Bill 2026

Moved to introduce the National Disability Insurance Scheme Amendment (Integrity and Safeguarding) Bill and have it read a first time without formalities; the question was agreed to and the bill was read a first time.
Defence Amendment (Defence Honours and Awards Appeals Tribunal) Bill 2025

Moved to remove the Defence Amendment (Defence Honours and Awards Appeals Tribunal) Bill 2025 from the Senate Notice Paper, arguing it would restrict veterans' and families' appeal rights and lacked support from the veterans community. The proceeding recorded support for withdrawal, further consultation and attention to recommendations of the royal commission into veteran suicides.
Environment Protection Reform Bill 2025

Tabled documents concerning orders for the production of documents about the Consumer Data Right, industry facilities at risk, the Environment Protection Reform Bill and incoming government briefs prepared by the Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water.
